It is Makkan.

In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–3} God Almighty swears by al-'Asr (time/the age), which is the night and the day, the place of the deeds and actions of the servants, that every human being is in loss. The loser is the opposite of the one who gains, and loss has many different degrees. It may be total loss, as in the case of one who has lost this world and the Hereafter, missed out on bliss, and deserved the Hellfire.

It may also be loss in some respects and not others. For this reason God made loss general for every human being, except for those who are characterized by four attributes:

Faith in what God has commanded us to believe in. Faith cannot exist without knowledge; it is a branch of knowledge and is not complete without it.

Righteous deeds. This includes all good deeds, outward and inward, whether they relate to the rights of God or the rights of His servants, and whether obligatory or recommended.

Mutual counsel to the truth, which is faith and righteous deeds; that is, they counsel one another to it, urge one another toward it, and encourage one another in it.

Mutual counsel to patience: patience in obeying God, patience in refraining from disobeying God, and patience with God's painful decrees. Through the first two matters a servant perfects himself, and through the last two he helps perfect others. By completing these four matters, the servant is safe from loss and attains the great gain.
